title: Add graceful shutdown with signal handling and request draining
description: Implements proper SIGINT/SIGTERM handling so the server stops accepting new connections, waits for in‑flight requests to finish, and exits cleanly after a configurable timeout. This improves reliability in containerized and production environments by preventing abrupt termination of active requests.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while a long‑running request is in progress and verify the server stops accepting new connections, allows the request to complete, then exits within the timeout
Trigger SIGINT with no active requests and ensure the server shuts down immediately and logs the shutdown sequence
acceptance: When the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, the framework logs a shutdown message, stops accepting new connections, waits up to the configured timeout for active requests to finish, then exits with code 0. If the timeout expires, it forcefully terminates remaining connections and exits with code 1. All logs follow the existing logging format and no unhandled promise rejections occur.
reason: Production deployments (especially in containers and serverless platforms) require deterministic shutdown behavior to avoid data loss and improve uptime. Adding graceful shutdown aligns Yantraverse with industry best practices and enhances its zero‑dependency, production‑ready promise.
